chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Milt throws rice in Chu Berry's saxophone and runs down Broadway
summary: Milt tells how he threw rice down Chu's horn three times and ran from the Cotton Club bandstand down Broadway with Chu chasing him.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Do you remember the incident between Chu Berry and I at the Cotton Club?

[LAUGHING] Boy, did I... We were on the stand, Danny Barker, Chu Berry, the band... And the Cotton Club show is going on. Now, this is in the middle of the show. And me, for reason... I had been out drinking, and I went to the kitchen and picked up a handful of dry rice and filled my tuxedo pocket with this dry rice out from the kitchen. And now, the saxophones are down front and the bass is in the back. And for some reason (God only knows now), I reached in there for a handful of rice, and threw it down the bell of Chu Berry's saxophone....
You know, he's playing... And Chu's this big pachyderm. You know, with all of him down there, he was hard as nails.

And he looked back at me, and took his horn and dumped the rice out. He said, 'Man, don't do that. Don't do that.' And I made ...(?)... (?)... to do some more. And they were dancing on the stage, and Cab was singing, and I threw another handful in there. And that time Chu Berry said, 'If you do that again, I'm gonna get up, and you know
where you're going..." -- (?)ing me, you know.

So the third time I did it, and he set his horn down. When he set his horn down, I set my bass down, ran off the bandstand, down Broadway, from Forty-Eighth Street and Broadway, Chu right behind me. I knew if he caught me, he'd kill me. But I was little and I could run. And right down Broadway we ran. I said, "I've got to keep ahead of him until I get him out of breath."

Well, I'll tell you, it took me... To get him out of breath, I was at Birdland. There was no Birdland then, but it was where Birdland was, 52nd Street. And when he got to 52nd Street he couldn't hardly breathe, and neither could I. Then he got... He couldn't even raise his hand. He said, "You better stop messin' with me." And we settled up, and I apologized, and we walked on back together.
